holidays.name: National Corned Beef and Cabbage Day
holidays.description: A salty, savory salute to the boiled dinner that takes over kitchen tables on St. Patrick's Day. Think tender corned beef, soft cabbage and potatoes, with a pint of something green nearby if you like.
holidays.origin: The day is an unofficial food observance that piggybacks on St. Patrick's Day. Irish immigrants in 19th-century America swapped pricey Irish bacon for cheaper corned beef from their Jewish and other immigrant neighbors. The meal became a tradition that stuck.
holidays.funFact: The word 'corned' has nothing to do with corn. It comes from the large 'corns' of rock salt once used to cure the beef.

holidays.name: Submarine Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate underwater vessels, from the first practical subs to today's deep-sea explorers. Watch a sub movie, build a model, or say a quiet 'ahoy' to anyone who lives below sea level for a living.
holidays.origin: The observance marks March 17, 1898. On that day, Irish-American inventor John P. Holland launched his submarine, the Holland VI. The U.S. Navy later bought it and made it the Navy's first commissioned submarine.
holidays.funFact: John P. Holland was born in Ireland, so the 'father of the modern submarine' has a perfect link to St. Patrick's Day.

holidays.name: Camp Fire Girls Day
holidays.description: A nod to the youth organization that has taught generations of kids about camping, crafts and community. Think s'mores, friendship bracelets and learning to build a fire safely.
holidays.origin: Camp Fire Girls was publicly launched on March 17, 1912. It was one of the first nonsectarian, multiracial youth organizations in America for girls. It later became Camp Fire and now welcomes all youth.
holidays.funFact: The group went co-ed in 1975 and is now simply called Camp Fire.
